title: DiaMedica shares signs that drug extends pregnancy in fetal growth restriction trial
summary: DiaMedica Therapeutics has shared phase 2 results in severe early-onset fetal growth restriction, reporting that most participants with known delivery dates remained pregnant longer than expected.

title: Why Iambic’s CEO believes preclinical cancer therapy could be ‘holy grail’ for CDK inhibitors
summary: Fresh off a $150 million IPO, Iambic Therapeutics has unveiled preclinical data for a potential challenger in one of oncology's most competitive drug classes: cyclin-dependent kinases.

title: FDA signs off on Siemens Healthineers next gen multiple sclerosis blood test
summary: The FDA has given de novo marketing authorization for Siemens Healthineers’ Atellica IM Neurofilament Light Chain (NfL) assay.

title: GE HealthCare launches ViewPoint Ultra to simplify ultrasound workflows
summary: GE HealthCare has launched ViewPoint Ultra, an ultrasound workflow solution designed to help health systems standardize clinical documentation and reporting across sites and departments while supporting specialized individual care needs.

title: Sanofi inks massive $41B Insmed buyout for post-Dupixent growth drivers
summary: Sanofi has struck a deal to acquire Insmed for $41 billion, securing three commercial and late-phase respiratory assets to offset Dupixent’s looming loss of exclusivity.

title: Exicure expands work into Parkinson’s with X-CUE smart glasses
summary: Exicure is partnering with NeuroQ Biologics and the South Korean medtech company Laonz to expand its business into medical device technologies designed to assist patients with Parkinson’s disease.

title: House panel pushes to reverse 'hollowing out' of US biotech amid China's rise
summary: The U.S. House Select Committee on China has published a report detailing policy recommendations to “reverse the hollowing out of the U.S. drug innovation industry.”

title: Kymera’s oral eczema drug impresses analysts with Dupixent-like phase 2 efficacy
summary: Kymera Therapeutics’ phase 2b eczema clinical trial has hit its primary endpoint and exceeded analyst expectations, teeing up further development of an oral drug candidate that could challenge Dupixent in a range of indications.

title: Arcus halts phase 3 pancreatic cancer study of CD73 inhibitor that looked destined to fail
summary: Arcus Biosciences has abandoned a phase 3 trial of quemliclustat after the small-molecule CD73 inhibitor looked unlikely to improve survival for pancreatic cancer.

title: Invivyd aims for Q1’27 submission after Pemgarda successor shows potential in phase 3
summary: Invivyd is planning to submit an approval application for its follow-up to the FDA-authorized monoclonal antibody Pemgarda in the first quarter of 2027 after hailing “high, durable antiviral activity” in a phase 3 trial.

title: Led by founders of J&J-acquired Intra-Cellular, Ritzey debuts with $112M for DYRK1A inhibitors
summary: The founder of Intra-Cellular Therapies, which was bought by Johnson & Johnson last year for $14.6 billion, is jumping back into the biotech fray with a new company similarly aimed at signaling pathways in the brain.

title: Lilly buys preclinical LoQus23 in $725M deal to zero in on Huntington’s target
summary: Eli Lilly has struck a deal to buy preclinical Huntington’s disease biotech LoQus23 Therapeutics for up to $725 million.

title: Capricor weathers second DMD cell therapy snub as FDA alleges 'serious' data integrity concerns
summary: Contrasting with the blunt release of the complete response letter that heralded the initial rejection of deramiocel last summer, the FDA appeared mindful of the optics Friday as it sought to explain why it turned down Capricor Therapeutics’ Duchenne muscular dystrophy cell therapy for a second time.

title: Danaher teams up with Microsoft to boost ‘experimental execution’
summary: Danaher Corporation and Microsoft are teaming up for a strategic partnership to develop smart scientific instruments and an interoperable agentic ecosystem.

title: Merck’s TROP2 ADC extends survival in pivotal gastroesophageal cancer trial
summary: Merck & Co.’s sacituzumab tirumotecan has improved overall survival in a phase 3 cancer trial, delivering a second pivotal global victory for the TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugate.

title: FDA pushes decision on Belite’s eye disease pill back to May
summary: The FDA is taking a little extra time to review Belite Bio’s application for its treatment for a rare genetic eye condition, pushing the expected action date back by three months into May next year.

title: ‘It’s a very healthy sector’: Biopharma gathers in London as M&A shines and China clouds loom

summary: On the same day Anthropic staged a record-shattering IPO on Nasdaq, the artificial intelligence tech giant’s lone pharmaceutical board member, Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan, was in London pitching investors on how the Swiss drugmaker is using AI to shrink drug development timelines and one day solve “biological latency.”

title: Crown Biosciences stays put as $204M Adicon deal falls through
summary: Crown Biosciences looks destined to go unworn for a while longer after its planned $204 million acquisition by China's Adicon fell through.

summary: Evaxion is refocusing its R&D efforts to solely focus on developing and advancing its cancer vaccines.

title: Self-Objectification Alters Brain Response to Media
summary: How does the way a woman views her own body shape how her brain responds to sexualized images in the media? Researchers found that higher self-objectification is linked to dampened neural activity in aesthetic judgment regions.

title: Brain Speech Hub Builds a “Blueprint” Before We Speak
summary: Textbooks have long taught that understanding speech and producing words happen in separate brain systems. A new study overturns that century-old model, revealing that a hub inside Wernicke's area builds an abstract "blueprint" for each word a quarter-second before we speak.

summary: How do microscopic soot and wildfire smoke particles injure the brain? Combining health records from 500,000 people with inhalation experiments, researchers foundPM2.5 air pollution raises dementia risk by 25% and reprograms brain immune cells.

title: Why We Slow Down With Age: Brain Serotonin Blocks Movement
summary: Why do we naturally move less as we grow older? Researchers discovered that the aging brain doesn't simply run out of fuel, instead, rising serotonin signaling acts like a biological brake on dopamine pathways that drive the urge to move.

title: Rice-Sized Wasp Brains Recognize Faces Just Like Humans
summary: With a brain the size of a grain of rice, the Northern paper wasp can tell individual nestmates apart by their faces. Researchers identified the specialized wasp neurons behind this feat, revealing neural computations remarkably similar to human facial recognition.

title: Blocking Gut Cannabinoid Receptors Restores Memory in Fragile X
summary: Can treating the gut restore memory in fragile X syndrome? Researchers discovered blocking peripheral cannabinoid (CB1) receptors outside the brain repairs the intestinal barrier, restores beneficial gut microbes, and improves hippocampal memory.

title: Brain’s Insula Shapes Pain, Emotion, and the Placebo Effect
summary: How do emotions and expectations change the way you feel physical pain? Drawing on 15 years of intracranial brain recordings across 87 patients, neuroscientists mapped four distinct regions of the human insula, uncovering a top-down circuit behind the placebo effect.

title: Screen Time and Fitness Reshape Grey Matter in Teen Brains

title: Ultraprocessed Foods Alter Food-Reward Brain Activity
summary: Even when calories, sugar, and fat are identical, industrial food processing changes how the young brain responds to food. A new study reveals that two weeks on an ultraprocessed diet blunts orbitofrontal cortex reward activity in adults ages 18 to 21.

summary: How does your brain instantly know which way a fast-moving object is heading? Using a new mapping tool across 46,000 brain cells, scientists discovered in Nature that the brain doesn't just take the eye's word for motion direction, specialized midbrain neurons compute it on their own.
